Effectiveness of a proficiency-based progression e-learning approach to training in communication in the context of clinically deteriorating patients: a multi-arm randomised controlled trial. article_title: Effect of head-mounted displays on students' acquisition of surgical suturing techniques compared to an e-learning and tutor-led course: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Peters Philipp, Lemos Martin, Bönsch Andrea, Ooms Mark, Ulbrich Max, Rashad Ashkan, Krause Felix, Lipprandt Myriam, Kuhlen Torsten W., Röhrig Rainer, Hölzle Frank, Puladi Behrus. (2023). Effect of head-mounted displays on students' acquisition of surgical suturing techniques compared to an e-learning and tutor-led course: a randomized controlled trial. International Journal of Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1097/JS9.0000000000000464
title: Prefer immersive stereoscopic HMD video over monoscopic web e-learning for surgical skills learning experience, while keeping practice volume central
description: The article concludes that "The use of HMDs with stereoscopic and immersive video provides advantages in enhancing the learning experience and should be preferred over a traditional web application for e-learning." HMD and e-learning courses were equally effective for skill gain, but the HMD course produced significantly better self-assessed improvement and suitability ratings, attributed to immersion, stereoscopy, and first-person perspective. Because feedback was not necessary for competence, self-directed HMD-based practice with high suture volume is a viable alternative to tutor-led teaching.
requirements: Stereoscopic 180° first-person video content; an adaptation period before HMD use; sufficient practice time with many suture repetitions.
constraints: The HMD course did not offer an interactive VR environment, only immersive stereoscopic video; HMD use beyond 30 min was rated neutral; conclusions about long-term retention cannot be drawn from this study.
target_learners: undergraduate medical and dental students (novices in suturing)
target_learning_goals: acquisition of basic surgical suturing technique
examples: In the RCT, students received a 40-min standardized theory session and 60-min practice on an EVA bench model; HMD students used an Oculus Quest 2 with a 180° stereoscopic first-person instructional video and could keep using it during practice.

citation: Usán Pablo, Salavera Carlos, Quílez-Robres Alberto, Lozano-Blasco Raquel. (2022). Behaviour Patterns between Academic Motivation, Burnout and Academic Performance in Primary School Students. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph191912663
title: Teachers should implement practices to prevent academic burnout to support performance and wellbeing
description: Based on the finding that burnout dimensions relate to motivation and performance, the authors recommend that schools act on burnout: "the study should encourage teachers to implement practices to prevent academic burnout and improve performance". They add that "educational programs should cultivate the psychological variables that lead to the harmonious development of the students' skills". The recommendation rests on the observed correlations between burnout, motivation, and marks in primary students.
requirements: Teacher awareness of burnout dimensions (exhaustion, cynicism, self-efficacy) and motivation profiles in their students
constraints: Derived from a cross-sectional study; the authors note data were collected at a single point in time so evolution of variables cannot be tracked
target_learners: Primary school students in the final two years of primary education
target_learning_goals: Academic performance and academic wellbeing
examples: The authors state that in practical terms the study should encourage teachers to implement burnout-prevention practices and that educational programs should cultivate the psychological variables supporting students' development

article_title: Student academic performance in non-lecture physiology topics following the abrupt change from traditional on-site teaching to online teaching during COVID-19 pandemic.
citation: Varachotisate P et al. (2022). Student academic performance in non-lecture physiology topics following the abrupt change from traditional on-site teaching to online teaching during COVID-19 pandemic. Medical Education Online. https://doi.org/10.1080/10872981.2022.2149292
title: Deliberately plan and utilise a variety of tools and techniques in online non-lecture classes to preserve interactivity
description: The article recommends that medical teachers "deliberately plan and utilise a variety of tools and techniques when developing online non-lecture classes to preserve the interactivity of the classes", which the authors suggest "might overcome this gap in students’ academic performance". In the study this meant Zoom breakout rooms and polls, Kahoot!, Mentimeter, Google Forms, and Google Sheets, yet students still reported reduced interaction.
requirements: Deliberate advance planning of online class activities and materials, as done in a 3-day staff seminar before the semester
constraints: Even with various online interactive tools, students reported decreased levels of interaction; the performance gap was not overcome in this study
target_learning_goals: non-lecture physiology topics including laboratory skills, physical examination, and discussion-based learning
examples: Online classes were organised using Zoom breakout rooms and polls, Kahoot!, Mentimeter, Google Forms, and Google Sheets to preserve interactivity

article_title: Curricular uptake of virtual gaming simulation in nursing education.
citation: Verkuyl M., Lapum J.L., St-Amant O., Hughes M., Romaniuk D. (2021). Curricular uptake of virtual gaming simulation in nursing education. Nurse Education in Practice. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nepr.2021.102967
title: Follow the process of prebrief, enactment, debrief and evaluation when using VGS
description: The article recommends structuring VGS use as a four-stage process: prebrief, enactment, debrief and evaluation. The prebrief sets the tone, articulates expectations, shares goals, orients learners to the environment, and clarifies evaluation; debriefing then supports reflection. The authors state "when using VGS, it is important to follow the process of prebrief, enactment, debrief and evaluation".
requirements: Dedicated prebrief time before the VGS occurs, including orientation to the virtual format, required technology, and technological support
constraints: Students learned less when they encountered technological challenges, so glitches must be averted through faculty familiarity and technical support
target_learners: practicing nurses and other healthcare professionals
target_learning_goals: clinical decision-making
application of learned concepts in realistic scenarios
examples: In the health assessment course, instructors provided a prebrief covering instructions, platform introduction, learning outcomes, grading, due date, and technological support before students played individually

article_title: Implementation of microsurgery simulation in an ophthalmology clerkship in Germany: a prospective, exploratory study.
citation: Deuchler Svenja, Scholtz Julia, Ackermann Hanns, Seitz Berthold, Koch Frank. (2022). Implementation of microsurgery simulation in an ophthalmology clerkship in Germany: a prospective, exploratory study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03634-x
title: Progressive simulator curriculum from abstract navigation tasks to clinical surgical modules
description: The Eyesi curriculum sequences practice from abstract to clinically specific: "Trainees begin with abstract Basic Navigation training and progress through different levels on the simulator, ending with more complex clinical skill modules." In this study, students "began with a basic skills targeting task (level 1 of the Eyesi module 'Navigation Training') and progressed through a maximum of 5 additional modules," with levels becoming "more specific to ophthalmologic surgical technique" as they advanced.
requirements: Simulator software with graded difficulty levels and objective scoring per level
An introductory lecture and demonstration before the first practical session
constraints: In this implementation only up to two sessions were available, so most students completed only the early abstract levels

target_learning_goals: controlled, precise instrument movement under the microscope
progression toward ophthalmologic surgical technique

article_title: Associations of physical activity with academic achievement and academic burden in Chinese children and adolescents: do gender and school grade matter?
citation: Zhang Danqing, Hong Jintao, Chen Sitong, Liu Yang. (2022). Associations of physical activity with academic achievement and academic burden in Chinese children and adolescents: do gender and school grade matter? BMC Public Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-022-13886-3
title: Promote physical activity among girls and middle school students to support academic achievement and reduce academic burden
description: The article concludes that promoting PA among girls or middle school students may be an effective lever for academic outcomes in the Chinese school context, because meeting the PA guideline was associated with above-average achievement in both genders and with reporting no academic burden specifically among girls and middle school students. It states "Promoting PA among girls or middle school students may be a good approach to improve AA and reduce AB." This is a recommendation the authors draw from their own stratified findings.
requirements: PA opportunities must allow students to reach at least 60 minutes of MVPA daily, the guideline threshold used in the study
constraints: The supporting evidence is cross-sectional and cannot infer bidirectional associations; the article recommends intervention, longitudinal or mediation studies to clarify the relationships

target_learning_goals: improving self-reported academic achievement
reducing felt academic burden
examples: In the study, participants were grouped by whether they reported at least 60 min MVPA daily across the previous week, and associations with achievement and burden were tested by gender and grade strata

citation: Kim Sunmi, Jeong Seok Hee, Kim Hee Sun, Jeong Young Ju. (2022). Academic Success of Online Learning in Undergraduate Nursing Education Programs in the COVID-19 Pandemic Era. Journal of Professional Nursing, 38, 6-16. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.profnurs.2021.10.005
title: Prioritize self-directed learning and manage satisfaction with online classes to achieve academic success in undergraduate online nursing education
description: The article's concluding design recommendation for online nursing education: educators should treat self-directed learning ability as a priority outcome and actively manage students' satisfaction with online classes, since both predicted achievement and satisfaction was driven by cyber-class flow. The article states: "To achieve academic success from online learning, self-directed learning should be prioritized and satisfaction with online class needs to be managed by nursing educators."
requirements: Students must take online classes in which they can steer their own learning environment, as the study's participants did in first-semester 2020 online nursing courses
constraints: Based on a cross-sectional correlational survey of 200 South Korean undergraduate nursing students; achievement was self-assessed, not objectively measured
target_learners: Undergraduate nursing students in online courses
target_learning_goals: Academic achievement in online nursing coursework
Satisfaction with online learning
examples: The survey measured self-directed learning, cyber-class flow, obstacles, satisfaction, and self-assessed achievement in 200 nursing students and ran hierarchical regressions identifying flow (β = 0.65) and self-directed learning (β = 0.18) as significant predictors

article_title: An upgrade of the Malmö model by implementing case-based teaching and learning, in an undergraduate dental education.
citation: Lundegren N, Jönsson A, Lindberg P. (2021). An upgrade of the Malmö model by implementing case‐based teaching and learning, in an undergraduate dental education. European Journal of Dental Education, 25(4), 649-656. https://doi.org/10.1111/eje.12642
title: Base high-stakes decisions on aggregated low-stakes assessments to track development towards clinical independence
description: The principle of programmatic assessment holds that assessment should be organised at the level of the whole programme, combining multiple low-stakes assessments whose aggregation informs high-stakes decisions such as credit awarding and progression. The article argues that "One single assessment can only address part of a student's competency, and no all‐encompassing assessment exists that can address all the aspects of student competency all at once." Low-stakes assessments should provide feedback for learning rather than grades, and repeated observations provide evidence of competence and progression and may stimulate reflection. The faculty is developing a digital assessment tool for continuous observation of students' development towards independence in clinical practice.
requirements: Several low-stakes assessments spread across the whole semester
A portfolio that can integrate multiple components for both low- and high-stakes use
constraints: Because summative assessment of professionalism is lacking, educators must actively produce clear expectations so the formative message does not conflict
target_learners: undergraduate dental students in clinical training
target_learning_goals: clinical independence
professionalism and professional approach
examples: Ongoing formative assessments of professionalism cover respect to peers, patients and faculty, integrity, responsibility, cooperation skills and punctuality

citation: Lohre Ryan, Leveille Lise, Goel Danny P. (2021). Novel Application of Immersive Virtual Reality Simulation Training: A Case Report. JAAOS Global Research & Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5435/JAAOSGlobal-D-21-00114
title: PrecisionOS immersive virtual reality surgical simulator with SCFE training module
description: PrecisionOS is an iVR simulator system used in this case for a severe SCFE percutaneous pinning module. It provides "a haptic-controlled virtual surgery, not only providing visual and auditory cues but also differentiating soft tissue and bone by sense of touch," simulated fluoroscopy for 3D guidewire localization, removable virtual pelvis and femur for close examination, full degrees of freedom, and performance metrics including the Precision Score.
requirements: Computer hardware interfaces including head-mounted displays and hand-based controllers providing haptic feedback
constraints: The Precision Score was validated as a performance metric in shoulder arthroplasty training, not specifically for SCFE
target_learning_goals: Virtual surgical skill acquisition
3D anatomical visualization and fluoroscopic localization
examples: The resident practiced guide pin insertion and screw placement with simulated fluoroscopy on interactive 3D anatomy, with metrics on performance and implant position observed.

article_title: Academic outcome and moderator of flipped classroom learning program "Teaching on the Run".
citation: Chen Kuo-Su, Hsieh Ming-Ju, Huang Min-Ping, Chen Chih-Ken, Hung Ming-Jui. (2021). Academic outcome and moderator of flipped classroom learning program “Teaching on the Run”. Biomedical Journal, 44(5), 636–643. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bj.2020.05.009
title: Facilitators of flipped classroom learning should promote strong pre-class achievement and high classroom engagement
description: Because achievement in pre-class learning (mid-test scores) predicted final knowledge gain and class participation moderated the mid-to-post score change, the article concludes that "facilitators should try their best to promote a good achievement in pre-class learning and engagement in classroom activity in FC style learning". Tutors are advised to prepare pre-class material carefully, assist learners before class, and teach in ways that attract interest and engagement.
requirements: Tutor preparation of pre-class material and assistance during pre-class learning; teaching that attracts student interest and engagement in classroom activities
constraints: The study is retrospective and non-controlled, so the exact impact of confounding variables cannot be examined without bias
target_learners: clinical teachers in flipped faculty development programs
target_learning_goals: teaching skills knowledge gain in flipped classroom learning
examples: The TOTR program assigned pre-class homework, monitored online learning with facilitator assistance, and reserved most classroom time for active learning such as discussion, teaching, presentation, exercise and sharing
key_sources: Chen Kuo-Su, Hsieh Ming-Ju, Huang Min-Ping, Chen Chih-Ken, Hung Ming-Jui. (2021). Academic outcome and moderator of flipped classroom learning program “Teaching on the Run”. Biomedical Journal, 44(5), 636–643. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bj.2020.05.009

article_title: Effectiveness of E-Learning Program in Preventing WP Smoking in Adolescent Females in West of Iran by Applying Prototype-Willingness Model: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
citation: Bashirian S, Barati M, Karami M, Hamzeh B, Ezati E. (2020). Effectiveness of E-Learning Program in Preventing WP Smoking in Adolescent Females in West of Iran by Applying Prototype-Willingness Model: A Randomized Controlled Trial. J Res Health Sci. 20(4): e00497. https://doi.org/10.34172/jrhs.2020.31
title: Prototype-Willingness Model as dual-path framework for adolescent health-risk behavior
description: The prototype-willingness model is the theoretical framework the study used to structure its questionnaire and intervention. It posits "two types of decision-making are involved in health behaviors": a logical-action path, where intention is predicted by attitude and subjective norms, and a social-reaction path, where "behavioral willingness can be predicted by risk prototype structure". The article applied it to water pipe smoking prevention among adolescent females, measuring all five constructs.
requirements: Measurement of attitude, subjective norms, prototype, behavioral willingness, and intention constructs as operationalized in the researcher-made questionnaire
constraints: The article applies the model to adolescent high-risk health behaviors; the social-reaction path concerns behaviors adolescents engage in without prior intention or program
target_learners: adolescent females in middle and high school
target_learning_goals: preventing water pipe smoking by reducing positive attitudes, subjective norms, smoker prototypes, intention, and behavioral willingness
examples: The trial's questionnaire measured all five model constructs with validated scales (Cronbach alpha 0.76–0.86), and the intervention targeted them across five sessions
key_sources: Bashirian S, Barati M, Karami M, Hamzeh B, Ezati E. (2020). article_title: "When in Doubt, Ask the Patient": A Quantitative, Patient-Oriented Approach to Formative Assessment of CanMEDS Roles.
citation: Esteves, A., McConnell, M., Ferretti, E., Garber, A., & Fung-Kee-Fung, K. (2021). "When in Doubt, Ask the Patient": A Quantitative, Patient-Oriented Approach to Formative Assessment of CanMEDS Roles. MedEdPORTAL. https://doi.org/10.15766/mep_2374-8265.11169
title: Integrate self-assessment measures with patient feedback in formal evaluations
description: The article recommends integrating self-assessment with patient feedback in formal evaluations to enrich learner experiences and improve patient outcomes. While the accuracy of self-assessment measures has been highly criticized in the literature, collecting self-assessment data along with patient assessments may provide unique opportunities for self-reflection and self-directed learning. The study's finding that self-scores were significantly lower than patient scores supports gap analysis between how trainees perceive themselves and how patients perceive them.
requirements: A validated tool such as the OCCAT that can be completed by both patients and trainees in first-person narrative form
Real-time completion following patient encounters
constraints: The accuracy of self-assessment has been criticized because individuals tend to overestimate their performance compared to a more objective measure
target_learning_goals: Self-reflection, metacognitive skills, and insight into intrinsic CanMEDS competencies
examples: In the study, the OCCAT was completed by patients and fellows following 70 unique encounters in an antenatal high-risk clinic, and the two rating sets were compared to identify incongruity
key_sources: Esteves, A., McConnell, M., Ferretti, E., Garber, A., & Fung-Kee-Fung, K. (2021). "When in Doubt, Ask the Patient": A Quantitative, Patient-Oriented Approach to Formative Assessment of CanMEDS Roles. MedEdPORTAL. https://doi.org/10.15766/mep_2374-8265.11169

article_title: A Health eLearning Ontology and Procedural Reasoning Approach for Developing Personalized Courses to Teach Patients about Their Medical Condition and Treatment.
citation: Michalowski Martin, Wilk Szymon, Michalowski Wojtek, O'Sullivan Dympna, Bonaccio Silvia, Parimbelli Enea, Carrier Marc, Le Gal Grégoire, Kingwell Stephen, Peleg Mor. (2021). A Health eLearning Ontology and Procedural Reasoning Approach for Developing Personalized Courses to Teach Patients about Their Medical Condition and Treatment. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph18147355
title: Precompiled-plan planning and execution framework for course sequencing and delivery
description: The framework adapts the Procedural Reasoning System (PRS) control architecture, using a planning and execution module, a goal stack, and a knowledge base. Precompiled plans specify a goal, optional preconditions, and a procedural body, and are used to sequence lessons within a course, sequence BUKs within a lesson, and control interaction with the patient. The plans are grouped into four levels, with single plans at Levels 1, 2 and 4 and two plans at Level 3 for delivering content and Q&A BUKs. The authors argue this "offers more flexibility and allows for more complex course strategies for course development and delivery than only rule- or ontology-based approaches."
requirements: Precompiled plans are processed by the planning and execution module and combined with knowledge-base content derived from the eLearning ontology
constraints: OWL does not natively support complex sequencing, which motivated the procedural reasoning approach
target_learners: patients receiving generated personalized courses in an outpatient setting
target_learning_goals: sequenced learning of condition and treatment knowledge matched to patient characteristics
examples: The planning and execution module is implemented in Python and uses the Owlready2 library to access the eLearning ontology stored in an OWL file

A Health eLearning Ontology and Procedural Reasoning Approach for Developing Personalized Courses to Teach Patients about Their Medical Condition and Treatment. article_title: Neurological, cognitive and learning evaluation of students who were born preterm.
citation: do Carmo André Luis Santos, Fredo Fernanda Wagner, Bruck Isac, de Lima Joseli do Rocio Maito, Janke Rebecca Nóbrega Ribas Gusso Harder, Fogaça Thais da Glória Messias, Glaser Jacqueline Andrea, Riechi Tatiana Izabele Jaworski de Sá, Antoniuk Sergio Antonio. (2022). Neurological, cognitive and learning evaluation of students who were born preterm. Revista Paulista de Pediatria. https://doi.org/10.1590/1984-0462/2022/40/2020252
title: Continue prematurity risk-clinic follow-up into school age with education and psychology professionals on the multidisciplinary staff
description: The article recommends that follow-up of preterm children in risk outpatient clinics should not stop at the preschool years but continue after schooling begins, because academic difficulties emerge at school age even in survivors without severe sequelae. It explicitly recommends that "education and psychology professionals be included in the multidisciplinary staff" conducting this follow-up, so that learning difficulties can be identified and addressed.
requirements: Follow-up clinics currently tracking preterm infants extend their monitoring beyond early childhood into the school years
Multidisciplinary staff include education and psychology professionals
constraints: Grounded in a cross-sectional single-clinic cohort without a term-born control group; the authors list reduced sample size and difficulty retrieving neonatal record data as limitations
target_learners: School-age children born preterm (6-14 years), especially those born extremely preterm
target_learning_goals: Early identification of reading, writing and mathematics difficulties and cognitive alteration in survivors of preterm birth
examples: The study assessed 83 preterm school-age children with a child neurologist, neuropsychologist and psychopedagogue, finding 59.1% with clinical school difficulties and high psychoeducational failure rates

article_title: The development and pilot testing of an ACP simulation-based communication-training program: Feasibility and acceptability.
citation: Chen Jui-O; Chang Shu-Chen; Lin Chiu-Chu. (2021). The development and pilot testing of an ACP simulation-based communication-training program: Feasibility and acceptability. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0254982
title: PREPARED model: an eight-step mnemonic communication guide for end-of-life discussions
description: The PREPARED model is a communication guide using the letters of PREPARED as a mnemonic for eight steps of discussing end-of-life topics, from preparing for the discussion and relating to the person, through eliciting preferences, providing information, acknowledging emotions, and encouraging questions, to documenting. The article states it is "a communication guide based upon the letters of PREPARED used as a mnemonic to help remember the eight steps" and used it to guide role-play practice in the ACP-SCT program. Debriefing, though outside the eight steps, is described as an indispensable part of the training process.
requirements: Used as a guide for structured communication practice with feedback and debriefing
constraints: Originally designed by Bristowe et al. for nephrology teams discussing end-of-life topics with ESRD patients
target_learning_goals: Structured communication about end-of-life care and advance care planning
examples: Participants took turns applying the PREPARED model in role plays with standardized patients across four simulation scenarios over Weeks 2 and 3
key_sources: Chen Jui-O; Chang Shu-Chen; Lin Chiu-Chu. (2021). The development and pilot testing of an ACP simulation-based communication-training program: Feasibility and acceptability. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0254982

article_title: The implementation of a flipped classroom approach at a UK dental school.
citation: Binnie Rebecca S. L., Bonsor Stephen J. (2021). The implementation of a flipped classroom approach at a UK dental school. British Dental Journal. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41415-021-3125-6
title: Protect timetable time for flipped pre-class preparation and budget staff time for recording and editing
description: The article warns that flipped preparation competes for student time and staff effort. If every course used this format, "the student may be overloaded and not have sufficient protected time to watch all of the lecture material", so "This preparatory, asynchronous material must be factored into the students' timetable." On the staff side, significant preparation time was required to record podcasts and there was a time-consuming learning curve with the software and editing skills, though pre-prepared material later saved lecturer time.
requirements: Asynchronous preparatory material must be factored into the students' timetable
Staff time and software training must be budgeted at start-up
constraints: Start-up costs of the investment of time are balanced only later by savings in lecturer time
target_learning_goals: preparation for in-class application activities
examples: The authors cite Chuang et al. and Patanwala et al. as reported cases where students lacked motivation or failed to view pre-recorded material, while in this course most students were engaged, attributed to clear direction via handbook and VLE
key_sources: Binnie Rebecca S. L., Bonsor Stephen J. (2021). The implementation of a flipped classroom approach at a UK dental school. British Dental Journal. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41415-021-3125-6

article_title: Understanding teaching and learning conceptions among clinical faculty as a means to improve postgraduate training.
citation: Pacifico JL, Donkers J, Jacobs J, van der Vleuten C, Heeneman S. (2020). Understanding teaching and learning conceptions among clinical faculty as a means to improve postgraduate training. International Journal of Medical Education, 11, 175-185. https://doi.org/10.5116/ijme.5f2a.76eb
title: Pratt's five perspectives on teaching as a framework for understanding clinical faculty conceptions
description: The article adopts Pratt's framework of five perspectives on teaching: transmission, apprenticeship, developmental, nurturing and social reform. A perspective is defined as "an interrelated set of beliefs and intentions that gives direction and justification to our actions." The article uses this framework to structure both the survey vignettes and the interview guide, finding that faculty readily embraced perspectives beyond transmission when introduced to them. The authors argue there is no single way to teach adults and call for "a plurality of perspectives on teaching that recognize and respect a diversity of teachers, learners, content, context, ideals, and purposes."
requirements: Teachers must be introduced to multiple perspectives (e.g., through vignettes) to become aware of alternatives beyond their default conception
constraints: Most teachers have one to two perspectives as their prevailing view, and the article notes it is superficial to assume the transmission perspective is the same as lecturing
target_learning_goals: understanding teaching conceptions
faculty self-awareness
teaching perspective development
examples: Vignettes summarizing the five perspectives were used in semi-structured interviews with 12 clinical teachers to elicit recognition and preference
key_sources: Pacifico JL, Donkers J, Jacobs J, van der Vleuten C, Heeneman S. (2020). Understanding teaching and learning conceptions among clinical faculty as a means to improve postgraduate training. International Journal of Medical Education, 11, 175-185. https://doi.org/10.5116/ijme.5f2a.76eb

article_title: Introduction of an ENT emergency-safe boot camp into postgraduate surgical training in the Republic of Ireland.
citation: Alabi Oludare, Hill Rhodri, Walsh Michael, Carroll Camilla. (2022). Introduction of an ENT emergency—safe boot camp into postgraduate surgical training in the Republic of Ireland. Irish Journal of Medical Science, 191(1). https://doi.org/10.1007/s11845-021-02581-8
title: Provide boot camp training before trainees commence posts, and sustain skills with ongoing access to structured simulation and deliberate practice
description: The article recommends that intensive simulation-rich boot camp training be delivered before trainees start posts in a craft specialty, because trainees "will benefit more from undergoing such training prior to commencement of such posts". It further states that "a boot camp model with subsequent provision of opportunities to access structured simulated training will provide the most long-term benefit", since gains fade without deliberate practice.
requirements: Subsequent provision of opportunities to access structured simulated training
Deliberate practice: structured practice focused on improvement rather than repetition, with real-time feedback
constraints: Long-term benefit is short-lived without clinical exposure to the scenarios or deliberate practice
Maintaining simulation equipment for constant practice is limited by available resources
target_learners: novice surgical trainees entering a new surgical training post
target_learning_goals: managing specialty-specific emergencies safely at the start of a training year
examples: The RCSI programme moved ENT emergency training from after commencement of the programme to a pre-commencement boot camp for all incoming CSTs
key_sources: Alabi Oludare, Hill Rhodri, Walsh Michael, Carroll Camilla. (2022). Introduction of an ENT emergency—safe boot camp into postgraduate surgical training in the Republic of Ireland. Irish Journal of Medical Science, 191(1). https://doi.org/10.1007/s11845-021-02581-8

article_title: Transfer of training-Virtual reality training with augmented multisensory cues improves user experience during training and task performance in the real world.
citation: Cooper Natalia, Millela Ferdinando, Cant Iain, White Mark D., Meyer Georg. (2021). Transfer of training—Virtual reality training with augmented multisensory cues improves user experience during training and task performance in the real world. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0248225
title: Prioritise informational effectiveness over surface fidelity when designing VR training with augmented multisensory cues
description: The article advocates that the primary emphasis in developing simulation-based training systems should be to maximize effectiveness, not necessarily fidelity, because high rendering quality is not always achievable. Augmented, information-bearing multisensory cues — visual colour changes, haptic vibration and auditory intensity signals — can carry task-critical information that is difficult to simulate realistically, such as torque and weight. The authors strongly encourage the use of such task-relevant, information-bearing cues during virtual training in future research.
requirements: Cues must be task relevant and information-bearing, signalling critical task states such as when a bolt is fully secured
constraints: The augmented cues reduce the overall realism or surface fidelity of the virtual environment during the training phase
target_learners: Trainees learning physical assembly or maintenance tasks that are costly or hazardous to practise in reality
target_learning_goals: Transfer of training from virtual to real environments and reduction of real-task errors
examples: The ATV group trained in VR with augmented auditory, tactile and visual cues completed the real tyre change with gains equivalent to 0.93 real tyre changes and received the fewest error penalties, compared with 0.37 equivalent sessions for conventional VR training
key_sources: Cooper Natalia, Millela Ferdinando, Cant Iain, White Mark D., Meyer Georg. (2021). Transfer of training—Virtual reality training with augmented multisensory cues improves user experience during training and task performance in the real world. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0248225

article_title: Framework for interprofessional case conferences - empirically sound and competence-oriented communication concept for interprofessional teaching.
citation: Posenau André, Handgraaf Marietta. (2021). Framework for interprofessional case conferences – empirically sound and competence-oriented communication concept for interprofessional teaching. GMS Journal for Medical Education. https://www.egms.de/en/journals/zma/2021-38/zma001461.shtml
title: Teach case-conference communication as a process-oriented procedure, not only as communication techniques or topic processing
description: The article argues that communication in case conferences must be taught as a process: knowledge of phases, processes and tasks is essential, and pure orientation to techniques is insufficient. Processing verbal and extra-linguistic tasks (ICF-oriented decision-making, goal-setting, leadership negotiation) is key; "the processing of topics alone is inadequate". Reflection on communication behaviour supplements the case conference itself.
requirements: Integration of process orientation and making communication relevant to goal achievement
Linking case content with communication development in contact time
constraints: Finding the right curricular place for bringing diverse professions together is a challenge; online formats can overcome spatial barriers
target_learners: health professions students in interprofessional modules
target_learning_goals: communicative competence for interprofessional teamwork
examples: The module goes beyond outcome development by integrating reflection on communication processes: not only 'What do we do?' but also 'How do we do it?'
key_sources: Posenau André, Handgraaf Marietta. (2021). Framework for interprofessional case conferences – empirically sound and competence-oriented communication concept for interprofessional teaching. GMS Journal for Medical Education. https://www.egms.de/en/journals/zma/2021-38/zma001461.shtml

article_title: To What Extent Do Study Habits Relate to Performance?
citation: Walck-Shannon, E. M., Rowell, S. F., & Frey, R. F. (2021). To What Extent Do Study Habits Relate to Performance? CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.20-05-0091
title: Prioritize active strategy use and focused study over study timing when advising students on exam preparation
description: Because active strategy diversity, proportion of active study time, and low distraction predicted exam scores while spacing potential did not, the article suggests instructors should "prioritize study habits to target for change" toward effortful, generative strategies and focused study sessions. The authors found that "both the degree to which students employed desirably difficult strategies while studying and their level of focus when doing so were important for performance," whereas starting earlier or studying over more sessions showed no relationship to performance.
requirements: Course context where students complete self-directed study and can choose among active strategies
constraints: The null timing result concerns spacing potential measures, not directly measured spacing of single topics; restudying before the final may have masked a spacing effect
target_learners: college students in large introductory STEM courses
target_learning_goals: exam performance and long-term retention of course material
examples: The course reopened weekly quiz questions near exam time and provided a first-week handout listing active study techniques with content-specific examples
key_sources: Walck-Shannon, E. M., Rowell, S. F., & Frey, R. F. (2021). To What Extent Do Study Habits Relate to Performance? CBE—Life Sciences Education. https://doi.org/10.1187/cbe.20-05-0091

article_title: The imperative of consistency and proficiency in cardiac devices implant skills training.
citation: Mascheroni Jorio, Mont Lluís, Stockburger Martin, Patwala Ashish, Retzlaff Hartwig, Gallagher Anthony G. (2021). The imperative of consistency and proficiency in cardiac devices implant skills training. Open Heart. https://doi.org/10.1136/openhrt-2021-001629
title: Proficiency-based progression (PBP): metric-based simulation training to a predefined proficiency benchmark
description: Proficiency-based progression is a training paradigm in which trainees must demonstrate a predefined proficiency benchmark, established from the quantified metrics of experienced implanters, before progressing to real patients. The article describes it as 'known as proficiency-based progression (PBP', an iterative process applied throughout training and for skill development on new procedures or devices, with simulation as the delivery vehicle. It 'ensures a more homogenous skillset, can be applied to any level of training'.
requirements: A detailed performance characterisation of the procedure with 'metrics' derived from expert consensus, scored with unambiguous operational definitions
A predefined proficiency benchmark set from experienced implanters' average quantified performance
constraints: The article states PBP 'is not meant to completely replace clinical in vivo training but aims to supplant a significant part of the initial learning curve on real patients'
target_learning_goals: Performing CIED implantation procedures at a predefined proficiency level
Consistent, quality-assured procedural skill
examples: Figure 1 presents PBP as an iterative process applied throughout and within training; a PBP scoresheet for lead fixation records whether each step was performed per definition, with errors or critical errors
key_sources: Mascheroni Jorio, Mont Lluís, Stockburger Martin, Patwala Ashish, Retzlaff Hartwig, Gallagher Anthony G. (2021). The imperative of consistency and proficiency in cardiac devices implant skills training. Open Heart. https://doi.org/10.1136/openhrt-2021-001629

article_title: Missed opportunities to prevent cardiovascular disease in women with prior preeclampsia.
citation: Brener A, Lewnard I, Mackinnon J, Jones C, Lohr N, Konda S, McIntosh J, Kulinski J. (2020). Missed opportunities to prevent cardiovascular disease in women with prior preeclampsia. BMC Women's Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12905-020-01074-7
title: Provider education slide deck delivered in person or by email with read-receipt
description: The intervention artifact was an educational slide presentation for internal medicine physicians on preeclampsia as a CVD risk factor, released as Additional file 2, plus a copy of the covering email (Additional file 3). The article states that "At clinics where in-person teaching sessions were not possible, the educational slide presentations (Additional file 2) were sent to physicians via email (Additional file 3) with a read-receipt link." The read receipt confirmed providers received the material but could not confirm review of the slides.
requirements: A delivery channel that reaches providers; the authors note emailed slide attachments may decrease engagement
constraints: The read-receipt served only as confirmation of receipt, not of individual participation or review; the intervention produced no significant change in screening documentation
target_learners: Internal medicine primary care physicians at academic-affiliated clinics
target_learning_goals: Educate providers on the significance of preeclampsia as a risk factor for cardiovascular disease
examples: Teaching sessions with Q&A were given at clinic sites; where in-person teaching was not possible, slides were emailed with a read-receipt link, and only 69% of email recipients opened them

article_title: 3D Versus 4K Display System - Influence of "State-of-the-art"-Display Technique on Surgical Performance (IDOSP-study) in Minimally Invasive Surgery: A Randomized Cross-over Trial.
citation: Wahba R, Datta R, Bußhoff J, Bruns T, Hedergott A, Gietzelt C, Dieplinger G, Fuchs H, Morgenstern B, Möller D, Hellmich M, Bruns CJ, Stippel DL. (2020). 3D Versus 4K Display System – Influence of “State-of-the-art”-Display Technique on Surgical Performance (IDOSP-study) in Minimally Invasive Surgery: A Randomized Cross-over Trial. Annals of Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1097/SLA.0000000000004328
title: Use 3D laparoscopic display rather than 4K for minimally invasive surgical training and performance, regardless of trainee expertise level
description: The article concludes that "3D laparoscopic display technique optimizes surgical performance compared to the 4K technique" and that "Surgeons benefit from the improved visualization regardless of their individual surgical expertise." Based on a randomized cross-over trial with 128 participants across three experience strata, it recommends 3D display for training Parkours and minimally invasive procedures where spatial orientation and rapid precise instrument movement matter.
requirements: Equipment for both 3D and 4K systems is expensive, so the choice must be justified; the benefit applies to tasks involving spatial orientation and fast precise instrument movement
constraints: In narrow spaces with low grades of instrument movement, 4K and 3D were comparable per the cited Harada et al work; in the trial 4K outperformed 3D only in the static precise "paper cut" task
target_learning_goals: minimally invasive laparoscopic surgical skills
spatial orientation in the operative field
reduction of performance time and mistakes
examples: In the IDOSP trial, participants performed 42 tasks (30 for MS) with each display system in randomized order, showing shorter time in 100% of tasks with 3D

article_title: Attitudes and concerns of undergraduate university health sciences students in Croatia regarding complete switch to e-learning during COVID-19 pandemic: a survey.
citation: Puljak Livia, Čivljak Marta, Haramina Ana, Mališa Snježana, Čavić Dalibor, Klinec Dinko, Aranza Diana, Mesarić Jasna, Skitarelić Nataša, Zoranić Sanja, Majstorović Dijana, Neuberg Marijana, Mikšić Štefica, Ivanišević Kata. (2020). Attitudes and concerns of undergraduate university health sciences students in Croatia regarding complete switch to e-learning during COVID-19 pandemic: a survey. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-02343-7
title: Deliver health sciences education as blended learning, with practical education in person, as the post-pandemic norm
description: The article proposes that health sciences programs combine face-to-face and online delivery rather than rely on either alone. From the survey findings, the authors conclude that "blended learning in health sciences, combining face-to-face and e-learning, where practical education will be delivered in person, might become the new norm, even after the COVID-19 pandemic". A combination of recorded and live-stream teaching is suggested to enable student-centered learning.
requirements: Practical education must be delivered in person; the article calls learning how to care for a patient a crucial part of health sciences education that is difficult to replace with online content.
constraints: Students showed no predominant opinion on feeling deprived or concerned about the lack of practical education, and many already worked in healthcare and expected to learn on the job.
target_learners: undergraduate university health sciences students in baccalaureate and master's programs
target_learning_goals: acquisition of practical patient-care skills alongside theoretical knowledge
flexible learning for employed and part-time students
examples: In the survey, 55.7% of students preferred a future combination of classroom and e-learning, and 63.8% of employed students agreed e-learning could complement classic classroom learning after the pandemic.

article_title: Identifying Entrustable Professional Activities for Shared Decision Making in Postgraduate Medical Education: A National Delphi Study.
citation: Baghus A, Giroldi E, Muris J, Stiggelbout A, van de Pol M, Timmerman A, van der Weijden T. (2020). Identifying Entrustable Professional Activities for Shared Decision Making in Postgraduate Medical Education: A National Delphi Study. Academic Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/ACM.0000000000003618
title: Process EPAs versus content EPAs as a distinction for competency-based workplace curricula
description: The article distinguishes process-oriented EPAs, which describe an underlying process of professional practice such as shared decision making that "may take place over several clinical encounters", from content-oriented EPAs, which are specific to a medical discipline (e.g., evaluating urinary incontinence in urology). The SDM EPAs are characterized as process EPAs and integrate competency domains such as medical knowledge, communication, collaboration, and EBM, translating generic competencies into the language of the profession to support focused observation and feedback in workplace learning.
requirements: Process EPAs must be distinguished from content-oriented EPAs specific to the medical discipline, and require context-specific application mapped to concrete clinical tasks
constraints: The distinction is drawn citing Warm et al's 2014 mapping study and a 2019 scoping review noting existing EPA development focused on specialty-specific EPAs
target_learning_goals: integration of complex competencies such as shared decision making into professional practice
examples: The authors position their 4 SDM EPAs as process EPAs that may support implementation of the specialty-specific EPAs catalogued in Shorey and colleagues' 2019 scoping review.
key_sources: Baghus A, Giroldi E, Muris J, Stiggelbout A, van de Pol M, Timmerman A, van der Weijden T. (2020). article_title: Developing Virtual Reality Trauma Training Experiences Using 360-Degree Video: Tutorial.
citation: Devika Patel, Jessica Hawkins, Lara Zena Chehab, Patrick Martin-Tuite, Joshua Feler, Amy Tan, Benjamin S Alpers, Sophia Pink, Jerome Wang, Jonathan Freise, Phillip Kim, Christopher Peabody, John Bowditch, Eric R Williams, Amanda Sammann. (2020). Developing Virtual Reality Trauma Training Experiences Using 360-Degree Video: Tutorial. Journal of Medical Internet Research. https://doi.org/10.2196/22420
title: Presence and PREality as two distinct psychological constructs underlying cineVR's psychological fidelity
description: The article distinguishes two psychological concepts from the virtual reality literature. "Presence" is defined as "a person's subjective sensation of being in a (usually virtual) scene, enabling them to interact with and feel connected to the world outside their physical bodies via technology." "PREality" is "designed to prepare the viewer for an anticipated experience by placing them in the actual environment where they intend to work," creating a sense of déjà vu. The article states that 360-degree videos do not need to be location-specific to create presence but do need to be location-specific to create PREality, and that the described production methods use both to establish a high level of psychological fidelity.
requirements: Creating PREality requires filming in the actual environment where the learner intends to work, i.e., location-specific video
constraints: Learners at other institutions will retain presence but will not obtain PREality from videos filmed at a different institution because of differing physical environments
target_learning_goals: familiarity with the trauma bay environment before real-life exposure
empathy with team-member perspectives
examples: The article cites prior work reporting that psychological fidelity is more important than physical fidelity in simulation training in other disciplines.

article_title: Relationship between fatness, physical fitness, and academic performance in normal weight and overweight schoolchild handball players in Qatar State.
citation: Hermassi Souhail, Chelly Mohamed Souhaiel, Michalsik Lars Bojsen, Sanal Nilihan E. M., D. Hayes Lawrence, Cadenas-Sanchez Cristina. (2021). Relationship between fatness, physical fitness, and academic performance in normal weight and overweight schoolchild handball players in Qatar State. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0246476
title: Promote physical fitness in pre-pubertal schoolchildren to support academic performance
description: The authors recommend promoting physical fitness in this age group because fitness components, particularly aerobic fitness, were positively associated with mathematics and science GPA, while fatness was negatively associated. They state "it seems pragmatic to promote physical fitness in this age group", via exercise or physical activity that could reduce excess adiposity. This recommendation rests on cross-sectional correlations, not intervention evidence.
requirements: Physical activity programming suitable for pre-pubertal schoolchildren, such as the handball training (about 4.2 h/week) the sample undertook
constraints: The cross-sectional design does not allow inference of temporality or causality; the authors state future intervention studies with large sample sizes are needed to corroborate the findings
target_learning_goals: mathematics and science academic achievement
examples: In the study, 36 handball players training about 3 times per week showed Yo-Yo IR1, jump, and T-half performance positively correlated with GPA, and BMI negatively correlated with GPA

article_title: What occupational therapists' say about their competencies' enactment, maintenance and development in practice? A two-phase mixed methods study.
citation: Rochette Annie, Brousseau Martine, Vachon Brigitte, Engels Cynthia, Amari Fatima, Thomas Aliki. (2020). What occupational therapists' say about their competencies' enactment, maintenance and development in practice? A two-phase mixed methods study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-02087-4
title: Profile of Occupational Therapist Practice in Canada: a seven-role competency framework
description: The Profile of Occupational Therapist Practice in Canada is a competency framework used for accreditation of university occupational therapy programs, described as "an equivalent to CanMEDS framework" for the profession. It comprises a central role, the expert in enabling occupation, surrounded by six transversal roles: communicator, collaborator, practice manager, change agent, scholarly practitioner and professional, each with key-competencies divided into enabling competencies. This study anchors its survey items, focus group probes and coding grid in the seven roles.
requirements: Used as the theoretical anchor for competency self-assessment and as an initial coding grid for qualitative analysis
constraints: Adapted from the CanMEDS framework developed for medicine; first published in 2007
target_learners: Occupational therapy students and clinicians with entry-to-practice master's degrees
target_learning_goals: Professional competence enactment, maintenance and development across seven practice roles
examples: The study rated survey respondents' perceived competency level for each of the seven roles and used the roles as focus group discussion areas
